Rashi on Shabbat 4b:1:1.hebrew: ובתוך י' - דאילו למעלה מי', לאו אויר ר"ה הוא, אלא אויר מקום פטור הוא, ואפי' קלוטה ליכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 4b:1:1.english: And within ten - For if [it were] above ten [handbreadths], it is not the airspace of a public domain, but rather it is the airspace of an exempt domain, and even [the rule of] kelutah [an object suspended in airspace] does not apply.

Rashi on Shabbat 4b:1:2.hebrew: זורק ממושיט - דאילו במושיט מרה"י לרה"י דרך ר"ה, אפי' למעלה מי', קיימא לן בפ' הזורק דחייב, דיליף מעגלות של מדבר שמושיטין את הקרשים מזו לזו, והן רה"י וביניהם ר"ה, ולא היו זורקים אותן שלא יתקלקלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 4b:1:2.english: Throwing from passing - For regarding one who passes [an object] from a private domain to a private domain via a public domain, even above ten [handbreadths], we hold in the chapter [entitled] "HaZorek" that he is liable, as it is derived from the wagons in the wilderness, where they would pass the beams from one [wagon] to another; and they were a private domain and between them was a public domain, and they would not throw them so that they would not get damaged.

Rashi on Shabbat 4b:4:1.hebrew: ודילמא הנחה הוא דלא בעיא - מדקתני ר"ע מחייב, אבל עקירה בעי מעל גבי מקום ד', מדלא קתני ר"ע מחייב שתים, אחת משום הוצאה ואחת משום הכנסה:
Rashi on Shabbat 4b:4:1.english: And perhaps placing is what does not require - [This is inferred] from the fact that it teaches: "Rabbi Akiva deems [him] liable." But lifting requires [lifting] from atop an area of four [handbreadths], from the fact that it does not teach: "Rabbi Akiva deems [him] liable for two: one on account of carrying out and one on account of bringing in."

Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:1:1.hebrew: אבל למעלה מי' ד"ה פטור - יש להוכיח קצת מכאן, דמושיט חייב נמי למטה מי'. דאם תמצא לומר פטור, לפי שלא מצינו במשכן מושיט למטה מי', שהעגלות היו גבוהים י', א"כ לימא הכא: אבל למעלה מי' ד"ה חייב, דילפינן זורק ממושיט? אבל עתה, דמושיט חייב למטה מי', אז לא מצי למימר למעלה מי' ד"ה חייב, דא"כ, למטה מי' מ"ט פטור זורק? ומיהו אינו הוכחה, דלא מצי למימר דלכ"ע ילפינן זורק ממושיט, דא"כ, הא דתנן לקמן בהזורק (שבת דף צו.): היו שתיהן בדיוטא אחת, הזורק פטור והמושיט חייב, אלמא לא ילפי' זורק ממושיט — אמאן תרמייה? ותדע, דהא כי נמי נימא דמושיט חייב למטה מי', הוי מצי למימר דלכ"ע ילפי' זורק ממושיט, ובדיוטא אחת, בין למטה מי' בין למעלה מי', ד"ה חייב, ופליגי למטה מי' בזו כנגד זו, דמר סבר אמרינן קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא, ומר סבר לא אמרינן. אלא דלא מצי למימר דלכ"ע ילפינן זורק ממושיט משום מתני' דהזורק. ולמאי שנפרש בסמוך, אתי נמי שפיר דלא נקט הכי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:1:1.english: However, above ten [handbreadths], everyone agrees he is exempt - One can bring a slight proof from here that [one who] passes [an object] is liable even below ten [handbreadths]. For if you were to say [that he is] exempt, because we did not find in the Tabernacle (Mishkan) [any instance of] passing below ten [handbreadths] — since the wagons were ten [handbreadths] high — if so, let [the Gemara] say here: "However, above ten [handbreadths], everyone agrees he is liable, as we derive throwing from passing"? But now that [one who] passes is liable below ten [as well], then it could not say "above ten [handbreadths], everyone agrees he is liable" — for if so, below ten, what is the reason that one who throws is exempt [according to the Rabbis]? However, this is no proof. For [the Gemara] could not say that according to everyone we derive throwing from passing — for if so, that which we learned in the mishna later in [chapter] HaZorek (Shabbat 96a): "[If] both of them were on the same level (bedeyota achat), one who throws is exempt and one who passes is liable" — which proves that we do not derive throwing from passing — according to whom would you attribute it? And know [that this is so], for even if we say that [one who] passes is liable below ten [handbreadths], [the Gemara] could [still] have said that according to everyone we derive throwing from passing, and [when the balconies are] on the same level, whether below ten or above ten, everyone agrees he is liable; and [rather,] they disagree below ten [handbreadths when they are] opposite one another (be-zo keneged zo), where one Master holds we say an object in airspace is considered at rest (kelutah kemi she-hunchah damya), and one Master holds we do not say [so]. Rather, [the reason] that it could not say that according to everyone we derive throwing from passing is [solely] because of the mishna in HaZorek. And according to what we will explain nearby [below, 4b:2], it also works out well why it did not formulate it this way.

Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:2:1.hebrew: דרבי עקיבא סבר ילפי' זורק ממושיט - וא"ת: והא ע"כ זורק מרשות היחיד לרה"י דרך רשות הרבים לא היה במשכן, דאם היה במשכן, מה צריך למילף ממושיט? ומ"ט נמי דרבנן דפטרי? וכיון דלא היה במשכן, אמאי מחייב ר"ע? דבתולדה דהוצאה, שהיא מלאכה גרועה, אין לנו לחייב אלא דוקא אותן שהיו במשכן, כדפרישית לעיל (שבת ד' ב.). וי"ל, דר"ע סבר דזורק דמי טפי למושיט, ממאי דדמו שאר תולדות להוצאה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:2:1.english: That Rabbi Akiva holds we derive throwing from passing - And if you say: But perforce, throwing from a private domain (reshut hayachid) to a private domain via a public domain (reshut harabbim) was not [performed] in the Mishkan; for if it had been in the Mishkan, why would it need to be derived from passing, and what also would be the reasoning of the Rabbis who exempt [it]? And since it was not in the Mishkan, why does Rabbi Akiva deem [one] liable? For regarding a subcategory (toledah) of carrying (hotza'ah), which is an inferior labor (melachah geru'ah), we should not hold [one] liable except specifically for those [actions] that were in the Mishkan, as I explained above (Shabbat 2a). And one can say that Rabbi Akiva holds that throwing is more similar to passing than other subcategories (toledot) are similar to carrying (hotza'ah).

Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:2:2.hebrew: אבל למטה מי' ד"ה חייב דאמר קלוטה כמי שהונחה - כשהחפץ בידו של עני או של בע"ה לא שייך קלוטה, דהא כשנותן בע"ה לתוך ידו והוציא לא מחייב. תימה לר"י: אם ברייתא היא בשום מקום דבעינן הנחה על גבי מקום ד', וכדמשמע קצת בסמוך דא"ר זירא: הא מני אחרים היא, משמע דפליגי רבנן עליה — אם כן, היכי קאמר הכא ד"ה חייב? אם כן, ההיא ברייתא מני? ונראה דלא קשה מידי, שיעמיד ר"ע ורבנן כמתניתין ולא כההיא ברייתא, דניחא ליה להעמיד מתני' ככ"ע. דאמרינן קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא - וקשה לר"י: דמאי פריך "למימרא דפשיטא ליה לרבה"? מנא ליה דפשיטא ליה לרבה? אי משום דקאמר "הא מני ר"ע היא", היינו משום דלר"ע אית ליה ממה נפשך קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא, אבל אליבא דרבנן מספקא ליה, ולהכי לא הוה מצי למימר "הא מני רבנן היא"! ואם היינו אומרים הא דקאמר לעיל "רבי עקיבא סבר קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא ורבנן כו'" הכל מדברי רבה היא — הוה אתי שפיר, אך אין נראה שיהא מדברי רבה. ואומר ר"י, דהכי פירושו: והא מיבעיא בעי לרבה, וכיון דאיכא לספוקי בפלוגתייהו, איכא נמי לספוקי דילמא לכולי עלמא לא אמרינן קלוטה כמי שהונחה, ובזו כנגד זו לכ"ע פטור, כי פליגי — בדיוטא אחת, דר"ע סבר: ילפי' זורק ממושיט, ורבנן סברי: לא ילפינן, אלא דרבה לא חש לפרש כל הבעיות. ועוד אומר ר"י, דהא דקאמר הש"ס: "אבל למטה מעשרה ד"ה חייב דאמרינן קלוטה כמי שהונחה" — היינו לרבנן, אבל לר"ע קלוטה לאו כמי שהונחה דמיא, ומחייב משום דילפינן זורק ממושיט. דאי סבר כמי שהונחה דמיא, לא הוה מצי למילף זורק ממושיט, דהא לא דמיא כלל! דכיון דכמי שהונחה דמיא, הוי [זורק למעלה מעשר'] כזורק מרה"י למקום פטור וממקום פטור לרה"י, ולא דמי כלל למושיט שהוא מרה"י לרה"י ורה"ר באמצע! אלמא ע"כ כיון דסבר ילפינן זורק ממושיט, סבר קלוטה לאו כמי שהונחה דמיא. והשתא אתי שפיר דפריך "למימרא דפשיטא ליה כו'", ואתי נמי שפיר דלא מצי למימר לעיל: "אבל למעלה מי' ד"ה חייב דילפינן זורק ממושיט", דלר"ע לא מצי למילף, כיון דסבר כמי שהונחה דמיא. וכן משמע קצת, דהא רב חסדא בעי נמי בהזורק (לקמן שבת דף צז.) כמו רבה דהכא, ואי הא דקא מסיים "קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא" קאי נמי אדר"ע, היכי מצי למימר לרב חסדא דלכ"ע כמי שהונחה דמיא? ולקמן בפירקין (שבת דף ח.) משמע דדוקא ברה"י לא בעי רב חסדא הנחה ע"ג מקום ארבעה. ומיהו רשב"א פירש בסמוך: אף ברה"ר לא בעי רב חסדא מקום ד':
Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:2:2.english: However, below ten [handbreadths], everyone agrees he is liable, as we say [that an object in airspace] is considered at rest - When the object is in the hand of the poor person or the homeowner, [the principle of] kelutah [an object suspended in airspace being considered at rest] does not apply [directly to it], for when the homeowner places [an object] into his [the poor person's] hand and he [the poor person] brings it out, he is not liable. The Ri finds it astonishing: If there is a baraita anywhere [stating] that we require placement onto an area of four [by four handbreadths]—and as is somewhat implied nearby, where Rabbi Zeira says (below, 5b): "Whose [view] is this? It is Acherim," which implies that the Rabbis disagree with him—if so, how can it say here that "everyone agrees he is liable"? If so, according to whom is that baraita? And it appears that this is not difficult at all: [Rabbah would] establish [both] Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis in accordance with our mishna, and not in accordance with that baraita, because it was preferable to him to establish our mishna in accordance with everyone. As we say [that an object in airspace] is considered at rest - And the Ri finds it difficult: Why does [the Gemara] object, "Is that to say that it is obvious to Rabbah...?" From where did [the Gemara] know that it was obvious to Rabbah? If [it inferred this] because he said, "Whose [view] is this? It is Rabbi Akiva," that is simply because according to Rabbi Akiva, mima nafshach (either way) he holds that an object in airspace is considered at rest, whereas regarding the opinion of the Rabbis he was in doubt; and for that reason he could not have said, "Whose [view] is this? It is the Rabbis"! And if we were to say that what was stated above—"Rabbi Akiva holds that an object in airspace is considered at rest, and the Rabbis, etc."—was entirely the statement of Rabbah, it would work out well; however, it does not appear that this was said by Rabbah. And the Ri says that this is the explanation: "And didn't Rabbah raise this as a dilemma?"—and since there is room for doubt regarding their dispute, there is also room to doubt that perhaps according to everyone we do not say that an object in airspace is considered at rest, and in [a case of two balconies] facing one another, everyone agrees that he is exempt; when do they disagree? [When they are both] on the same storey (deyota), where Rabbi Akiva holds that we derive throwing from passing, and the Rabbis hold that we do not derive [throwing from passing]—it is merely that Rabbah did not bother to detail all [possible sides of] the dilemma. And furthermore, the Ri says: That which the Talmud stated, "However, below ten [handbreadths] everyone agrees he is liable, as we say [that an object in airspace] is considered at rest"—this is [only] according to the Rabbis; but according to Rabbi Akiva, an object in airspace is not considered at rest, and he deems him liable because we derive throwing from passing. For if he [Rabbi Akiva] held that it is considered at rest, he could not have derived throwing from passing, for they are not comparable at all! For since it is considered at rest, [throwing above ten handbreadths] would be like one who throws from a private domain into an exempt domain (makom patur), and from an exempt domain into a private domain, which is not comparable at all to passing, which is from a private domain to a private domain with a public domain in the middle! It follows perforce that since he holds we derive throwing from passing, he holds that an object in airspace is not considered at rest. And now it works out well that [the Gemara] objects: "Is that to say that it is obvious to him, etc.?" And it also works out well why it could not say above: "However, above ten [handbreadths] everyone agrees he is liable, as we derive throwing from passing"—for according to Rabbi Akiva, he could not derive [throwing from passing], since he holds that it is considered at rest. And this is also somewhat implied [by the fact] that Rav Chisda also raises a dilemma in [the chapter] HaZorek (below, Shabbat 97a) just like Rabbah here; and if that which concludes, "an object in airspace is considered at rest," also applied to Rabbi Akiva, how could it say according to Rav Chisda that everyone agrees that an object in airspace is considered at rest? For further on in our chapter (Shabbat 8a) it implies that only in a private domain does Rav Chisda not require placement onto an area of four [handbreadths]. However, the Rashba explained nearby that even in a public domain Rav Chisda does not require an area of four [handbreadths].

Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:4:1.hebrew: ודילמא הנחה הוא דלא בעיא הא עקירה בעיא - פירש"י דדייק מדלא מחייב ב', אחת משום הוצאה ואחת משום הכנסה. וקשה: דילמא הא דלא מחייב ב' משום דלא מחייב אתולדה במקום אב? ועוד, דבסמוך קאמר רב יהודה: מחייב היה רבי ב', אע"ג דקתני סתם רבי מחייב, ה"נ לר"ע, מנ"ל דלא מחייב שתים? ונראה לפרש, דפריך: הא עקירה בעיא, דילפינן ממשכן, שהיו נוטלין מתיבתן שהיו בהן ארבע על ארבע, ונותנין ליד עושי המלאכה. ולפי מה שפירשתי לעיל, דדרשינן מאל יצא איש ממקומו, אתי נמי שפיר דבעקירה מיירי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:4:1.english: And perhaps placing does not require [it], but lifting requires [it] - Rashi explains that [the Gemara] infers this from the fact that [the mishna] does not deem him liable for two [sin-offerings] — one on account of carrying out (hotza'ah) and one on account of carrying in (hachnasah). But this is difficult: perhaps the reason he is not liable for two is because one is not liable for a derivative labor (toldah) alongside a primary category (av)? And furthermore, nearby (below, 4b), Rav Yehuda says: "Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] would deem him liable for two," even though [the baraita] plainly teaches "Rabbi deems him liable" [in the singular]. Here too, regarding Rabbi Akiva, from where do we know that he does not deem him liable for two? And it seems [preferable] to explain that [the Gemara] challenges: lifting surely requires [an area of four by four], for we derive [this] from the Mishkan (Tabernacle), where they would take [items] from their chests, which measured four by four [handbreadths], and place them into the hands of the craftsmen. And according to what I explained above (4a), that we derive [the requirement of an area of four by four] from "Let no man go out of his place" (Exodus 16:29), it also works out well, since [the verse] is dealing with lifting.

Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:5:1.hebrew: אלא א"ר יוסף כו' - קשה לרשב"א: מה צריכין רבה ורב יוסף להעמיד המשנה כתנאים? והא סבירא להו בפ"ב דעירובין (ד' צט. ושם) דמחשבתו משויא ליה מקום, דקאמר התם רב יוסף: השתין ורק חייב חטאת, ופריך: והא בעינן מקום ד' וליכא, ומשני: מחשבתו משויא ליה מקום, דאי לא תימא הכי, הא דאמר רבה: זרק בפי כלב או בפי כבשן חייב וכו'. ותי' ר"ת, דהא דאמר מחשבתו משויא ליה מקום, היינו היכא דלא ניחא לי' בענין אחר אלא בענין זה, כמו משתין ורק שאינו יכול להשתין או לרוק בענין אחר, וכן זרק בפי כלב שרצונו שיאכלנו הכלב, או שישרוף העץ בכבשן. ול"ג התם ונח בפי כלב, דנח משמע דאין כוונתו לכך. אבל הכא, אינו חושש אם מקבל בידו או בכלי אחר. והא דאמר לקמן (שבת ד' ה.) ה"א ה"מ היכא דאחשבה לידו, אע"ג דניחא ליה שיקבלנו בע"א כמו בידו — היינו משום דקאמר דידו של אדם חשובה לו כד' על ד', אבל בשאר דברים לא משוי ליה מחשבתו אלא היכא דלא ניחא ליה בע"א:
Tosafot on Shabbat 4b:5:1.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said, etc. - The Rashba raises a difficulty: Why do Rabba and Rav Yosef need to establish the mishna in accordance with [individual] Tannaim? For don't they maintain in the last chapter of Eruvin (99a and there) that one's intention designates it as a place [of four by four handbreadths]? For Rav Yosef said there: One who urinated or spat [from a private domain into a public domain] is liable to bring a sin-offering. And it objects: But don't we require an area of four [by four handbreadths], and there is none? And it answers: His intention designates it as a place. For if you do not say so, [what of] that which Rabba said: One who threw [an object] into the mouth of a dog or into the mouth of a furnace is liable, etc. And Rabbeinu Tam answered that this statement that "his intention designates it as a place" applies only where it is not satisfactory to him in any other way but this way — such as one who urinates or spits, who cannot urinate or spit in any other way, and likewise one who threw into the mouth of a dog, where his desire is that the dog should eat it, or that [the fire in] the furnace should burn the wood. And we do not hold the reading there: "and it landed in the mouth of a dog," since "and it landed" implies that this was not his intention. But here [in our mishna], he does not care whether he receives it in his hand or in another vessel. And as for that which [the Gemara] says below (Shabbat 5a): "I might have said that this applies [only] where he deemed his hand significant" — even though it would be just as satisfactory to him to receive it in another way as in his hand — that is because it says that a person's hand is considered for him like four by four [handbreadths]; but with regard to other things, his intention does not designate it [as a place] unless it is not satisfactory to him in any other way.
